itens.t: Israel Election Exit Polls Signal Deadlock as Neither Netanyahu Nor Rival Secures Majority
itens.r: Israel's first general election since October 7 has resulted in a tight deadlock, according to exit polls released late Tuesday. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor his primary opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, are currently on track to secure an outright parliamentary majority. High voter turnout was reported across the country, with Arab-majority parties notably surging to a projected record number of seats. President Isaac Herzog will ultimately task the candidate best positioned to form a coalition once official results are finalized.
itens.d:
Israel's first election following the events of October 7 appears to be deadlocked. Exit polls indicate that neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot is currently on track to secure a majority.

The political landscape remains uncertain as the country waits to see how the final results will unfold and whether a stable government can eventually be formed from the divided outcome.

High international oil costs, currency depreciation, and structural adjustments in the labor market are contributing to the challenge. These combined factors could make it harder for the Central Bank to meet its targets.

itens.t: Astronomers Discover Lava Exoplanet Equipped with Natural Solar Shield Reflecting 75% of Light
itens.r: Researchers observing the lava exoplanet TOI-561 b discovered that its unique atmospheric or surface properties reflect approximately 75% of incoming stellar radiation. This high albedo prevents the celestial body from completely melting under extreme heat.
itens.d:
Astronomers recently observed the lava exoplanet TOI-561 b for thirty-seven hours as it completed four orbits around its host star. The planet was found to reflect approximately seventy-five percent of the starlight it receives without melting.

Scientists attribute this unusual phenomenon to a natural solar shield composed of silicate mineral clouds. This barrier reflects stellar radiation before it can fully impact the surface of the rocky exoplanet.
